Of course. Here is a parent-facing guide written in plain, accessible language that explains the move to mixed-attainment teaching in mathematics.

***

### **Helping Every Child Succeed in Maths at [School Name]**

Dear Parents and Carers,

We are writing to you about an important and positive change we are making to our maths lessons. We know how much you care about your child’s education, and we want to share our plans with you.

Starting next school year, we will be moving to what are called **‘mixed-attainment’** groups for maths.

This simply means that instead of grouping children into different classes based on what we think their ‘ability’ is (sometimes called ‘streaming’ or ‘sets’), your child will be in a maths class with students who are all at different stages in their learning.

We know this is a big change, and you will probably have questions. Many of us grew up with streaming, so it’s natural to wonder why we are moving away from it. We want to explain our reasons and, most importantly, how this will help your child.

#### **Why Are We Making This Change?**

Our single most important job is to make sure every child can succeed. After looking at a lot of research and our own experience in the classroom, we are confident that this new way of teaching is the best way to help every student build their confidence and skills in maths.

Here are the main reasons why:

**1. It builds confidence and a ‘can-do’ attitude.**
When we put children in ‘bottom’ or ‘middle’ sets, they can quickly start to believe that they are bad at maths. This can damage their confidence for years. In a mixed group, no one is labelled. Every child is shown that they are capable of succeeding.

**2. It helps everyone learn from each other.**
In a mixed class, students get to talk about maths and solve problems together.
*   Students who find a topic tricky get to hear it explained by their classmates in a different way.
*   Students who are more confident in a topic get to deepen their own understanding by explaining it to others. Teaching someone else is one of the best ways to really learn something.

**3. It sets higher expectations for all students.**
In the old system, students in some sets were sometimes not given the chance to try the most challenging work. In our new classes, every child will be given the same chance to tackle interesting, challenging problems. We will not put a ceiling on what your child can achieve.

**4. It’s better preparation for life.**
In the real world and in the workplace, you have to work with people with all sorts of different skills and strengths. Learning to work together in the classroom is great practice for the future.

---

### **Answering Your Questions**

We know you may have some worries. Here are our answers to the most common questions.

**“Will my child, who is a high-flyer, be held back or get bored?”**

No. In fact, we believe they will be challenged even more. Instead of just rushing ahead to the next topic, they will be challenged to think more deeply about the maths they are doing.

For example, the teacher won’t just ask, “What is the answer?” They will ask, “Can you prove it? Can you find a different way to solve it? Can you create a similar problem for your friend?” This builds a much deeper, more secure understanding of maths, which is essential for future success.

**“Will my child, who struggles with maths, be left behind?”**

Absolutely not. They will get more support, not less. They will be in a classroom where it’s okay to make mistakes and ask questions. They will get support from the teacher and from their classmates.

Being in a room where other students are feeling positive about maths is a huge boost. They won’t be stuck in a group where everyone feels like they can’t do it, which we know can be very discouraging.

**“How can one teacher possibly teach 30 children at all different levels?”**

This is a great question. Our teachers are being specially trained for this way of teaching. A mixed-attainment classroom looks a bit different:

*   The teacher will plan tasks that **everyone can start, but that can be stretched** for those who need a bigger challenge.
*   There will be more **teamwork and problem-solving in pairs and small groups**.
*   The teacher will move around the room, checking in with individual students and small groups, providing support and extra challenges where needed.

Our goal is simple: to help every single child develop their confidence and skills in maths, and to enjoy it too. We truly believe this is the best way to do that.

We are excited to start this journey with you and your child. If you have more questions, we would love to talk to you.

We will be holding a **Parent Information Evening** on [Date] at [Time] in the school hall. We will share more examples of what the lessons will look like and answer all of your questions.

In the meantime, please feel free to speak to [Name of Headteacher] or [Name of Head of Maths].

Thank you for your support.

Sincerely,

[Your Name/School Name]
